lead: St. Paul plumbing is built for deep cold, old homes and basements. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across St. Paul.
risk: lead service lines, frozen pipes and basement plumbing in older homes
risk_short: lead lines, frozen pipes and basements
why: Summit Hill, Macalester-Groveland, Merriam Park and Dayton's Bluff have many homes from the 1880s to the 1930s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines.
Long, deep winters freeze pipes near exterior walls and can freeze water service lines. Nearly every home has a basement with the water heater, floor drain and laundry.
water: St. Paul's water comes from the Mississippi River, a chain of lakes and wells, and is softened at the plant. The utility is replacing lead service lines across the city.
tips: Check the water utility's lead line lookup.
Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Test your sump pump before spring thaw.
areas: PipeMend works in Summit Hill, Highland Park, Macalester-Groveland, Como, Frogtown, the West Side, Dayton's Bluff and every other St. Paul neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the St. Paul Department of Safety and Inspections, and plumbers must be licensed by the Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry.

faq.q: Is St. Paul replacing lead water lines?
faq.a: Yes. Saint Paul Regional Water Services has a program to replace lead service lines across the city, often at little or no cost to owners. You can look up your address on its website.
